holds.reason: This is a 2008 Crescent City harbor and approach survey. Its descriptive report identifies significant channel shoaling, numerous uncharted rocks along the southern offshore edge, and incomplete full-bottom coverage of the approach. The five eligible 4 m screen cells overlapping a predicted-hard polygon (about 80 square meters) cannot establish a natural fishing reef or a safe approach. Keep the survey for harbor-source review; do not promote it to a fishing target without a current chart, site-specific original-cell review and separate substrate evidence.

The 2009 Stil Well Point–Greenwood Cove survey contains fine measured depth and historical rocky-camera overlap, but its original report identifies five dangers to navigation, charted rocks/islets needing correction, and holidays where least depths were not established. The NOAA NBS sample has 60 locally qualified rocky-camera windows, yet only 18 also pass the strict 25 m original-BAG native-grid and depth screen; 37 are held at original fine-grid edges. Do not promote a Fort Bragg–Point Arena target until hazards are reconciled with the current ENC, exact source footprints and position uncertainty are reviewed, and local species/method rules and access pass separately.

The 2008–2009 Point Delgada survey is the measured contributor behind a North Mendocino NOAA NBS test tile with 46 historically rocky camera windows passing the tile's 25 m screen, but only three also pass the original 242 MB BAG's fine-grid/depth/uncertainty neighborhood screen; 43 are held near original fine-grid edges. Its final descriptive report identifies seven dangers to navigation, two rocks of unknown depth over shallow shoal holidays, charted-islet corrections and dynamic sediment bottom. Withhold the survey from fishing-target promotion until current ENC hazards, exact substrate and MPA footprints, access and Mendocino rules are reconciled. The tile and 2010 camera records alone do not locate a present fishable reef.

The 2009 Big White Rock–Abalone Point survey contributes measured cells to another North Mendocino NOAA NBS test tile. Of 35 tile-qualified historical rocky-camera windows, only seven pass the exact original 222 MB BAG fine-grid/depth/uncertainty neighborhood screen; 25 are held at original fine-grid edges and three fail original cell qualification. Its report identifies four dangers to navigation and chart contour and shoal discrepancies, including a 10-fathom contour displaced by as much as 400 m in an older chart comparison. Keep the survey as a source lead, not a fishing target, until the current ENC, historical hazards, exact substrate and MPA footprints, access and Mendocino rules are reviewed.
